Listening 2 — Fill in the Blanks (in class)
"Hi everyone, it's Charlotte! Last weekend I visited an onsen in Hakone for the first time, so here are my top tips."

"First, you wash your body before you get into the bath. Everyone does it — no exceptions."

"Second, you put your towel in the water. I almost did!"

"Third, you don't have to bring your own towel — most places rent them. And finally, you should drink plenty of water afterwards."

"I didn't, and I felt dizzy all evening. I really more water! See you next time!"
📖
Listening 2 Vocabulary Note
no exceptions
Everyone must follow the rule; nobody is different.
例外なし
dizzy
Feeling that everything is spinning and you might fall.
めまいがする、くらくらする

Dialogue Practice — Ondoku
オーディオを聞いて、繰り返し音読練習をしましょう。ハイライト語句にカーソルを当てると日本語が表示されます。
DIALOGUE AUDIO
Mai & Charlotte — Bridge Café
Mai
Charlotte, do you have a minute? I have to do an interview for a hotel internship next week — all in English.
Charlotte
Mai, that's amazing! Congratulations!
Mai
Thanks, but I'm so nervous. Do I have to wear a suit?
Charlotte
For a hotel, you definitely should. First impressions really matter in hospitality.
Mai
Okay. Should I memorize all my answers?
Charlotte
No, you don't need to. Just prepare a few good stories. But you mustn't be late — hotels are really strict about time.
Mai
Got it. What if I don't understand a question?
Charlotte
Then just ask them to repeat it. At my first interview, I guessed and gave a strange answer. I should have asked!
Mai
(laughs) Okay, you've convinced me. Could you practice with me this weekend?
Charlotte
Of course! Let's do a mock interview on Saturday.
EXPRESSIONS EXPLANATION
first impressions
The opinion people form when they meet you for the first time.
第一印象
hospitality
The business of hotels, restaurants, and serving guests.
ホスピタリティ業界、接客業
strict about ~
Making sure a rule is always followed.
～に厳しい
You've convinced me.
Your reasons made me agree with you.
納得したよ、あなたの言う通りにするよ
mock interview
A practice interview to prepare for the real one.
模擬面接

会話のアイデアを英語で書いてみましょう。
Someone from overseas has just joined your workplace, school, or club. They ask you what they need to know. Tell them the rules, what they don't need to worry about, and give some friendly advice.
Think about the conversation you would have and write down your ideas below.

e.g. You don't have to worry about wearing a suit.
